title: Run cross-built Go test binaries on native Windows
applies_when: A pure-Go package has OS-dependent path, filesystem or error-classification behavior, and an authorized Linux build host plus a native Windows execution target are available. Source and test dependencies must be independently inspected and runnable in task-private directories.
lesson: Use a pinned Go toolchain to cross-build the real package test executable with CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -c -o fs.test.exe ./package. Bind the source revision plus test bytes, verify the transferred executable hash, then actually run it on native Windows with task-private TEMP/TMP. Compare unchanged baseline and repair using the identical regression, and retain a Linux control. Cross-compilation alone cannot expose runtime separators. For a separately executed binary, a reviewed official cmd/test2json converter can feed the existing go-json reader: test2json -t -p PACKAGE fs.test.exe -test.v=test2json. Verify both executables and record their toolchain versions. Check flag support; plain -test.v has lower fidelity. Prefer go test -json when a native compiler is available. Preserve parent/subtest identities and the package terminal, rather than counting PASS-looking stdout lines. A standalone test executable does not carry external testdata: use a reviewed package working directory with hash-verified fixtures. Preserve missing-fixture failures; rerun the identical binary with the correct runtime inputs rather than patching production or dropping tests. For ZIPs, assert archive entry names from a nested directory source; archiving one file may retain only its basename and miss the recursive join. Keep archive-internal path.Join separate from filesystem filepath.Join, but do not infer a defect from the import alone: afero's index and lookup both normalize with filepath, and the original issue395 archive passes on current Windows source. A focused pass does not erase an unchanged broader-suite failure: record its baseline/candidate result and test inventory separately. Inspect hosted CI commands before treating a green badge as a platform witness: Afero PR700's successful AppVeyor log only shows go version and test discovery, not a test invocation or results. Also inspect the observation channel: Windows newline translation and a test's subsequent CRLF normalization can change a correctly preserved data value. For CR-sensitive regressions, compare values before rendering or print lossless predicates rather than sending the witness through another normalizer. Keep normal newline controls; do not skip Windows or change production only to satisfy the test printer.
avoid_when: Do not disable cgo to pretend that a cgo-dependent production path was tested; cross-builds can exclude files and require a C cross-compiler or target libraries. Match target architecture and OS capabilities, check source and test safety before execution, and do not start local WSL or install global tools merely to reproduce this workflow. An application-control denial is unexecuted, not test failure or permission to rename/move/re-route the binary. Evidence covers a goraven Go1.27.2 repair and scoped afero Go1.26.9 negative witnesses, not full application/CI, all archives, old runtimes or universal Windows support. The permission checks do not recreate the 2022 reporter's runtime/dependency versions, its Afero.WriteFile wrapper reproduction or pkg/errors assertions. No claim of measured cost savings, PR acceptance, recall or throughput follows from the method.

evidence.note: Official single-binary JSON conversion, -p package attribution and -test.v=test2json framing. Conversion is not execution or source verification; go test -json is preferred when available.

Official Go guidance distinguishes cross-building pure-Go Windows executables from running them on Windows, describes initial standard-library build/cache cost, and warns that cgo inputs can be excluded. Mechanism documentation, not a measured result.
FileHeader.Name requires relative forward-slash paths. This archive format contract differs from native filesystem path separators.

Submitted source-bound Root.Zip regression: nested archive names fail on native Windows before the path.Join repair and pass after; Linux core/fs tests pass on both. The test binary was built on Linux with Go1.27.2 and executed on Windows. An existing leading-slash return-path assertion fails unchanged in the broader Windows package run and is explicitly disclosed. Publication is not maintainer acceptance or full application qualification.

Scoped owner feedback: unchanged eb6a928, Windows/amd64 Go1.26.9 CGO=0, original attached ZIP and three directory/file controls pass. Existing zipfs tests also pass after supplying their original runtime fixtures. Three first-run failures were missing testdata from the executable's working directory; the same binary succeeds with verified fixtures. Not a full root-module, race, old-version or every-archive claim.

splitpath, index construction and lookup use consistent filepath normalization. This is not writing native separators into archive FileHeader.Name; check the actual producer/consumer contract before transferring the goraven repair.

Hosted PR700 head80658d58: successful two-second Windows job logs Go1.13.3 version and test discovery, with no go test command or results. This badge does not close the disclosed Windows runtime gap; GitHub Actions separately awaits maintainer approval.

Current-runtime counterexample: unchanged eb6a928 on Go1.26.9 Linux and native Windows/amd64 recognizes EPERM through os.IsPermission and errors.Is for 14 rejected ReadOnlyFs mutations, with read, missing-file and direct-runtime controls. The Windows binary was cross-built, hash-verified, then executed; each platform has 18 passing parent/subtest events, not 18 independent defects. This is not the original 2022 dependency stack or the complete Afero suite.

The inspected current wrapper still returns syscall.EPERM. That unchanged return statement and an open old issue do not establish a current permission-classification failure; test the effective runtime rather than blindly replacing the error type.

TestCSVMultiRead applies normalizeNewlines to captured output only on Windows; normalizeNewlines replaces CRLF with LF. This public source establishes an oracle transformation to inspect, not acceptance or complete qualification of a new CSV repair.
